response.sql:
WITH joined AS (
  SELECT e.ordersmark, o.timespan, e.fillcount,
    AVG(e.fillcount) OVER (PARTITION BY o.timespan) AS tif_fill
  FROM orderexecutions e
  JOIN orders o ON e.ordersmark = o.recordvault
),
order_avg AS (
  SELECT ordersmark, timespan, MAX(tif_fill) AS tif_fill, AVG(fillcount) AS avg_fill
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY ordersmark, timespan
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT ordersmark, timespan, avg_fill, tif_fill,
    avg_fill - tif_fill AS excess,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY timespan ORDER BY avg_fill DESC NULLS LAST) AS fill_rank
  FROM order_avg
)
SELECT ordersmark, timespan, avg_fill, excess, fill_rank
FROM ranked
WHERE avg_fill > tif_fill AND fill_rank <= 3
ORDER BY timespan, fill_rank, ordersmark;

assumptions.assumption: Each orders.recordvault value identifies exactly one order row, so the join adds no duplicate execution rows.
Time-in-force figure is the plain average of fillcount over all matched execution rows for that timespan, with NULL fillcount values ignored; it is not an average of per-order averages.
Each order's average fill ignores NULL fillcount values; an order whose executions all have NULL fillcount has no average and is excluded by the strict comparison.
Orders with a NULL timespan form one group together, and their ranks and time-in-force figure are computed within that group.

Ranks are computed over all orders in each time in force, not only those above the average. This does not change the result, because orders at or below the average always rank below those above it, and NULL averages sort last via NULLS LAST.
